book: Nancy Caroline · Chapter 19 · Communications and Documentation
title: Reports, Hand-overs and Records: Proving What the PCP Did
next: Chapter 20: Trauma Systems and Mechanism of Injury

slides.title: Today's lesson
slides.body:
As an EMR you already give radio reports, hand over at the bedside, and write a PCR. Now, as a PCP:

  1. Report in a fixed order that includes everything you did
  2. Document every IV, drug and reassessment so the record proves it
  3. Handle and record refusals, including a “no” to one intervention

Textbook: Chapter 19, PDF pages 1606–1668
slides.say: Welcome to class. Today's chapter isn't about a disease; it's about the words that travel with your patient. As EMRs, you already know how to call the hospital, hand over at the bedside, and write a patient care report, or PCR. So why does this matter more now? Because as a PCP you do more: IVs, fluids, new drugs. Every one of those has to be reported, timed, reassessed, and written down, or the next team can't build on it. Today we'll cover three things: a report order that includes your PCP care, documentation that proves what you did, and refusals, including a refusal of just one part of your care.
slides.sayZh: 欢迎来上课。今天这章讲的不是某种病，而是跟着病人一起交出去的话和文字。作为 EMR，你们已经会呼叫医院、在床旁交接、写患者照护报告，也就是 PCR。那为什么现在更重要？因为作为 PCP 你做得更多：静脉通路、补液、新的药物。每一项都必须报告、记下时间、复评、写下来，否则下一个团队没法接着做。今天讲三件事：包含你 PCP 处置的报告顺序；能证明你做过什么的文书记录；以及拒绝治疗，包括只拒绝其中一项处置。

slides.title: On the air: clear, private, confirmed
slides.body:
• Listen first; hold the key 1 second before you talk
  • Call them, then you: “City General, this is Medic 12”
  • Mic 5–8 cm away; calm voice; 30-second chunks
  • Risky numbers: whole, then digit by digit
  • No patient names on air: anyone may be listening
  • Orders: echo back drug, dose, route; ask if unclear
slides.say: Let's warm up with radio skills you already use. Listen before you talk, hold the key for at least a second, and call the other unit first, then give your own name, so they're already listening when you identify yourself. Keep the microphone five to eight centimetres from your mouth, stay calm, and break long messages into thirty-second chunks. Say risky numbers twice: 'saturation eighty-five, that's eight-five.' Never say the patient's name; scanners can pick up radio and even cell phone calls. Here's the PCP part: when direct medical control gives you an order, echo it back, the drug, the dose and the route, and ask, 'Is that confirmed?' If anything is unclear, ask again before you give it.
slides.sayZh: 先用你们本来就会的无线电技巧热热身。说话前先听频道是否空闲，按住发射键至少一秒再开口；先呼叫对方，再报自己，这样对方在你报名时已经在听了。麦克风离嘴五到八厘米，语气平稳，长信息拆成三十秒一段。容易听错的数字说两遍：「血氧八十五，八-五」。绝不在电台里说病人姓名，扫描器能监听无线电，甚至手机通话。PCP 的部分在这里：直接医疗指导给你医嘱时，要把药名、剂量、途径复述一遍，再问「确认吗？」任何地方没听清，给药前再问一次。

slides.title: The report: same order every time
slides.body:
1. Age, sex and chief complaint
  2. Brief history of this problem
  3. Relevant past history: conditions, medications, allergies
  4. Level of consciousness and distress
  5. Vital signs, then key findings head to toe (ECG if done)
  6. Treatment given and the response

Gather it, sort it in your head, then call. A good report takes under 30 seconds.
slides.say: The textbook gives a standard order for a medical report, and the order matters more than your style. Start with age, sex, and chief complaint. Then a short history of this problem, then the past history that matters: major conditions, medications, and allergies. Next, level of consciousness and how distressed the patient is, then vital signs and the key findings from head to toe. Last comes treatment and the response. For you, that last line is now longer. For example: 'IV started, right forearm, D10W twenty-five grams given, patient now alert, glucose six point one.' Gather everything first, sort it in your head, then call. A good report takes under thirty seconds.
slides.sayZh: 教材给出了医疗报告的标准顺序，顺序比说话风格更重要。先说年龄、性别和主诉；再说这次问题的简要经过；然后是相关的既往史：重大疾病、用药和过敏。接着是意识水平和痛苦程度，然后是生命体征和从头到脚的关键体检发现。最后是已给的处置和病人的反应。对你来说，最后这一行现在更长了，比如：「右前臂建立静脉通路，给 D10W 二十五克，病人现已清醒，血糖六点一。」先把信息收集齐，在脑子里理顺，再呼叫。一份好的报告不到三十秒。

slides.title: Bedside hand-over: SBAR
slides.body:
SBARWhat you say
Situationwho you are, the patient, chief complaint, MOI
Backgroundhistory, medications, allergies
Assessmentimpression, vitals, exam, treatment given
Recommendationwhat you think is needed now

Hand over only to someone at your level or higher. Add what the radio report missed.
slides.say: At the hospital, the radio report becomes a bedside hand-over. Many hospitals and EMS services use SBAR. S is Situation: who you are, who the patient is, the chief complaint and the mechanism of injury. B is Background: past history, medications, allergies. A is Assessment: your clinical impression, vital signs, exam findings, and the treatment you gave. R is Recommendation: when it applies, what you think should happen next. Remember the patient can hear you, so step aside or lower your voice for sensitive details. Add anything the radio report left out. And hand over only to someone at your level of care or higher; otherwise you risk abandonment.
slides.sayZh: 到了医院，无线电报告就变成床旁交接。很多医院和 EMS 机构用 SBAR。S 是现况：你是谁、病人是谁、主诉和受伤机制。B 是背景：既往史、用药、过敏。A 是评估：你的临床印象、生命体征、体检发现和已给的处置。R 是建议：适用时，说出你认为接下来该做什么。记住病人听得到，敏感内容要走到一边或压低声音说。补上无线电报告里没说的内容。而且只能交给与你同级或更高级别的人，否则有遗弃的风险。

slides.q: You're the PCP. En route you started an IV and gave a 500 mL bolus; the heart rate fell from 124 to 108. Where does this go in your radio report?
options: First, before age and sex, because it's the most important
Last: what you gave, how much, and how the patient responded
Leave it out; the hospital will see the IV when you arrive
Only mention it if the blood pressure went up
slides.say: Let's check. You're the PCP. On the way in, you started an IV and gave a five-hundred-millilitre bolus, and the heart rate fell from one hundred twenty-four to one hundred eight. Where does this go in your radio report? A, first, before age and sex, because it's the most important. B, last: what you gave, how much, and how the patient responded. C, leave it out; the hospital will see the IV when you arrive. D, only mention it if the blood pressure went up. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来检查一下。你是 PCP，途中建立了静脉通路，给了五百毫升的补液，心率从一百二十四降到一百零八。这些内容在无线电报告里应该放在哪里？A 放最前面，在年龄性别之前，因为最重要；B 放最后：给了什么、给了多少、病人有什么反应；C 不用说，到了医院他们自然看得到静脉通路；D 只有血压升高了才提。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. Treatment and the response always come last in the standard order, and for a PCP that means the IV, the volume given, and what changed. A breaks the order, and a listener who expects a fixed order is more likely to miss things. C is wrong because the receiving team needs to know how much fluid is already in. D is wrong because a falling heart rate is a response worth reporting, and so is no change at all.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。按标准顺序，处置和反应永远放在最后；对 PCP 来说，就是静脉通路、已输入的量和病情变化。A 打乱了顺序，听的人习惯固定顺序，反而更容易漏听。C 错在接收团队需要知道已经输进去多少液体。D 错在心率下降本身就是值得报告的反应，完全没有变化也同样要报告。

slides.title: Document every intervention
slides.body:
“Followed protocol” is not documentation

  • IV: site, catheter size, fluid, volume, every attempt
  • Drug: name, dose, route, time, who ordered it
  • The patient's response, good or bad
  • Orders and consults: written out in the narrative
  • Never just “see refusal on back”
slides.say: Now the written record. The textbook warns that writing 'followed protocol' is not enough. Your medical director wants specifics. For an IV: the site, the catheter size, the fluid, the volume, and every attempt, not just the one that worked, because services count skills attempted and performed. For a drug: the name, dose, route, time, and who ordered it if it came from direct medical control. Then the response, good or bad. Orders and consults belong in the narrative, written out in full, never 'see back'. Why so strict? Because your PCR is often the only record of why you gave a drug. If it isn't written, you can't prove you did it.
slides.sayZh: 现在讲书面记录。教材提醒：只写「按流程处理」是不够的，你的医疗主任要的是具体内容。静脉通路：部位、留置针型号、液体种类、输入量，以及每一次尝试，不只是成功的那一次，因为机构会统计技能的尝试次数和成功次数。药物：药名、剂量、途径、时间，如果是直接医疗指导下的医嘱，还要写是谁下的。然后写反应，好的坏的都写。医嘱和会诊要在叙述部分完整写出来，绝不能只写「见背面」。为什么这么严？因为 PCR 往往是你为什么给这个药的唯一记录。没写下来，就无法证明你做过。

slides.title: Times that now drive your decisions
slides.body:
• Call, dispatch, arrival, patient contact
  • The time of each drug you give
  • Leaving scene, arrival at hospital, back in service
  • Check your times against dispatch

PCP link: BC gives no TXA more than 3 hours after injury, so record when it happened. Note every tourniquet time too.
slides.say: Times are part of the legal record. The textbook lists the key ones: the call, dispatch, arrival on scene, patient contact, each medication, leaving the scene, arrival at hospital, and back in service. Patient contact can come well after arrival, for example when the patient is in a basement suite at the back of a long property. Dispatch keeps most of these times, so check yours against theirs. As a PCP, times now drive decisions. In BC, TXA isn't given more than three hours after the injury, so ask when it happened and write it down. And BC tells every licence level to note the time a tourniquet goes on. Without the right time, you can't make the right drug decision.
slides.sayZh: 时间是法律记录的一部分。教材列出的关键时间有：接警、派车、到场、接触病人、每次给药、离开现场、到达医院、恢复待命。接触病人的时间可能比到场晚很多，比如病人住在一块很深的地块尽头的地下室套间里。这些时间大多由调度记录，所以要把你的时间和调度核对。作为 PCP，时间现在会左右你的决定。在 BC，受伤超过三小时就不给 TXA，所以要问清什么时候受的伤，并写下来。BC 还要求所有级别记录止血带上好的时间。时间不对，就做不出正确的用药决定。

slides.title: Reassess, then record it
slides.body:
BC protocols build reassessment into your care

  • IV running: ABCs, vitals and IV site about every 5–15 min
  • Fluid bolus: reassess every 500 mL
  • Naloxone: reassess at 3 minutes before the next dose
  • Chest pain: vital signs every 5 minutes
  • Oxygen: record SpO₂ changes as you treat

A drug that isn't written down may be given again at hospital.
slides.say: Reassessment is where PCP documentation really grows, and the BC protocols build it in. When an IV is running, the IV maintenance procedure says to reassess regularly, about every five to fifteen minutes: the ABCs, injury sites, vital signs, and the IV site, tubing and bag. With a fluid bolus, you reassess every five hundred millilitres. With naloxone, you reassess at three minutes before the next dose. In chest pain, vital signs every five minutes. And with oxygen, record how the saturation changes as you treat. Each of those checks belongs in the PCR. The textbook gives the reason: if a drug isn't documented, the hospital may give it again, and the patient gets too much.
slides.sayZh: 复评是 PCP 文书记录真正增加的地方，BC 流程把它写进去了。静脉输液时，静脉维护流程要求定期复评，大约每五到十五分钟一次：气道呼吸循环、受伤部位、生命体征，以及穿刺部位、管路和液袋。补液时，每五百毫升复评一次。给纳洛酮后，三分钟时复评，再决定下一剂。胸痛病人，每五分钟测一次生命体征。给氧时，记录血氧随处置的变化。每一次复评都要写进 PCR。教材讲了原因：药没记下来，医院可能再给一次，病人就会用药过量。

slides.title: Writing the narrative
slides.body:
Chronologicalthe call as a storydispatch to finish
SOAPSubjective, Objective, Assessment, Plansimple and logical
CHARTEComplaint, History, Assessment, Treatment, Transport, Exceptionsfollows your assessment
  • Pick one format and stick to it
  • Pertinent negatives: what you checked that was normal
  • Quotes: exact words, in quotation marks, and who said them
slides.say: The narrative is the story part of your PCR. The textbook names a few formats. Chronological tells the call as a story, from dispatch to finish. SOAP stands for subjective, objective, assessment, and plan. CHARTE stands for chief complaint, history, assessment, treatment, transport, and exceptions, and it follows the order of your assessment. A body-systems approach exists too, but it's slow in the field. Choose one and stick with it; switching halfway is how details get lost. Record pertinent negatives, the things you checked that were normal, such as 'denies shortness of breath'. They prove your exam was complete. And when you quote someone, use their exact words in quotation marks and say who said them.
slides.sayZh: 叙述部分是 PCR 里讲故事的部分。教材列了几种格式。时间顺序法：从派车到结束，像讲故事一样写。SOAP：主观、客观、评估、计划。CHARTE：主诉、病史、评估、治疗、转运、例外，和你的评估顺序一致。还有系统法，但在院前写起来很慢。选一种就一直用，写到一半换格式最容易漏东西。要记录相关阴性，也就是你查过、结果正常的内容，比如「否认气短」，它证明你的检查是完整的。引用别人的话时，用原话加引号，并写明是谁说的。

slides.title: Refusals: all of your care, or one part
slides.body:
• Capable: oriented to person, place and time; makes sense
  • Informed: risks in plain words, including death
  • Witness: name and contact recorded
  • Documented: assessment, baseline vitals, the discussion
  • Clearly needs care? Call direct medical control
  • Not transported: written follow-up plan; they can call back

Refusing one intervention, like an IV, is handled like any refusal.
slides.say: You've handled refusals as an EMR. As a PCP you'll meet a new kind: a patient who accepts transport but refuses one part of your care, like an IV. The textbook says to treat that exactly like any refusal. Four pieces. Capable: oriented to person, place and time, and making sense, with no low blood sugar, injury or intoxication behind the refusal. Informed: you explain the risks in plain words, including death. A witness, whose name and contact you record. And documentation: your assessment, a full set of baseline vital signs, and the discussion. If the patient clearly needs care, contact direct medical control. If they stay home, leave a written follow-up plan, and tell them they can call back any time.
slides.sayZh: 拒绝治疗你当 EMR 时就处理过。作为 PCP，你会遇到一种新情况：病人同意转运，却拒绝其中一项处置，比如静脉通路。教材说，这要完全按拒绝治疗来处理。四个要素。有行为能力：对人、地点、时间定向清楚，说话合乎逻辑，拒绝的背后没有低血糖、外伤或醉酒等因素。充分告知：用通俗的话讲清风险，包括死亡。见证人：记录其姓名和联系方式。记录：你的评估、一整套基线生命体征，以及谈话经过。如果病人明显需要救治，联系直接医疗指导。如果病人留在家里，留下书面随访计划，并告诉他们随时可以再打电话。

slides.q: A capable patient with chest pain agrees to transport but refuses the IV you offer. What should your PCR show?
options: The risks you explained, the patient's signed refusal of the IV, a witness, and the full discussion
Nothing; the patient still went to hospital
slides.say: Here's a documentation question. A capable patient with chest pain agrees to transport but refuses the IV you offer. What should your PCR show? A, just 'refused IV'. B, the risks you explained, the patient's signed refusal of the IV, a witness, and the full discussion. C, nothing, because the patient still went to hospital. D, 'see refusal on back'. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来一道文书记录题。一位有行为能力的胸痛病人同意转运，但拒绝你提出的静脉通路。你的 PCR 应该写什么？A 只写「拒绝静脉通路」；B 你讲过的风险、病人签字拒绝静脉通路、见证人，以及完整的谈话经过；C 什么都不用写，反正病人去了医院；D 写「拒绝书见背面」。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. The textbook says refusing one procedure is handled like any refusal: explain the risks, get the patient's signature for that part of care, have a witness, and document it completely. A records the decision but not that it was informed. C is wrong because refusing part of your care still needs a record. D is wrong because the textbook says 'see back' is not proper documentation; the discussion belongs in the narrative.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。教材说，拒绝某一项操作要按拒绝治疗同样处理：讲清风险，请病人就这一部分照护签字，安排见证人，并完整记录。A 只记了决定，没有证明是知情的。C 错在拒绝部分照护同样需要记录。D 错在教材明确说「见背面」不是合格的记录，谈话经过要写在叙述部分。

slides.title: Mistakes, late entries, lost reports
slides.body:
One line through it→Initial and date→Correct entry beside it
  • No erasing, scribbling, correction fluid or tape
  • Only the author revises; never destroy the original
  • Addendum: marked as added, with reason, date, time, signature
  • No personal copies; never re-create a lost PCR
slides.say: Everyone makes mistakes on a PCR; what matters is how you fix them, because it's a legal document. On paper, draw a single line through the error, initial and date it, and write the correct entry beside it. No erasing, scribbling, correction fluid or tape. Only the person who wrote the report can revise it, and the original is never thrown away. If you forgot something important, for example a second dose you gave, write an addendum. Mark it as added, and include the reason it's late, the date, the time and your signature. Don't keep personal copies of reports, and never try to re-create a lost one; the textbook calls that irresponsible and possibly illegal.
slides.sayZh: PCR 人人都会写错，关键是怎么改，因为它是法律文件。纸质报告上，在错误处画一条横线，签姓名缩写和日期，在旁边写上正确内容。不能擦、不能乱涂、不能用涂改液或修正带。只有原作者能修改报告，原件绝不能丢掉。如果漏写了重要内容，比如你给的第二剂药，就写一份补遗：注明是补充内容，写明迟记的原因、日期、时间并签名。不要私留报告副本，也绝不要试图重写一份丢失的报告；教材说这样做不负责任，还可能违法。

slides.title: What the PCP actually does
slides.body:
All licence levels (EMR + PCP)

  • Clear radio report in a fixed order
  • Bedside hand-over to equal or higher level
  • Times, findings, pertinent negatives
  • EMR drugs: dose, route, time, response
  • Refusals: capable, informed, witnessed, written

PCP adds

  • IV: site, size, fluid, volume, attempts
  • PCP-only drugs, like D10W, ondansetron, TXA
  • Reassessment on schedule: IV, every 500 mL
  • CPAP or PEEP settings and the response
  • Functional enquiry findings (PCP only)
  • Refusals of PCP care, like an IV
slides.say: So what actually changes for you? The left side is what every licence level does: a clear radio report in a fixed order, a bedside hand-over to someone at your level or higher, accurate times and findings with pertinent negatives, the drugs EMRs already give, documented with dose, route, time and response, and properly handled refusals. The right side is new. You now document IVs: site, catheter size, fluid, volume, and attempts. You give PCP-only drugs, such as D10W, ondansetron and TXA, each with its own record. You reassess on schedule and write it down. If you use CPAP or a PEEP valve, record the settings and the response. You add the functional enquiry, a PCP-only part of the history. And you'll document refusals of your new interventions.
slides.sayZh: 那你的工作到底变了什么？左边是所有级别都做的：按固定顺序做清楚的无线电报告；床旁交接给同级或更高级别的人；准确记录时间、发现和相关阴性；EMR 本来就给的药，记录剂量、途径、时间和反应；正确处理拒绝治疗。右边是新的。你现在要记录静脉通路：部位、留置针型号、液体、输入量和尝试次数。你会给 PCP 专属药物，比如 D10W、昂丹司琼和 TXA，每一种都要单独记录。你要按时复评并写下来。如果用了 CPAP 或 PEEP 阀，要记录设置和反应。你要加上系统问诊，这是 PCP 独有的病史部分。还要记录病人对你这些新处置的拒绝。

slides.title: New for you as a PCP: watch out for
slides.body:
• A drug or bolus not written down may be given again
  • “IV started” alone tells the next team nothing
  • Count every attempt, not just the success
  • No time of injury? You can't judge the TXA 3-hour limit
  • An order you didn't echo may be an order you misheard
  • Handing PCP care to a lower level risks abandonment
slides.say: Here are the new traps. First, the overdose trap: a drug or fluid bolus you didn't record may be given again at the hospital. Second, a vague entry like 'IV started' doesn't tell the next team the size, the site, or how much went in. Third, count every attempt, not only the successful one; your service tracks skills attempted and performed. Fourth, if you never asked when the injury happened, you can't judge TXA's three-hour limit. Fifth, an order you didn't echo back may be an order you misheard, and one wrong number in a dose is a medication error. And sixth, once you've started PCP-level care, handing it to someone with less training risks abandonment.
slides.sayZh: 下面是新的陷阱。第一，过量陷阱：没记录的药或补液，到医院可能被再给一次。第二，像「已建立静脉通路」这样含糊的记录，下一个团队看不出型号、部位和输了多少。第三，每一次尝试都要记，不只是成功那次，机构会统计技能的尝试和成功次数。第四，如果你从没问过什么时候受的伤，就没法判断 TXA 的三小时时限。第五，没复述的医嘱可能就是听错的医嘱，剂量错一个数字就是用药差错。第六，一旦开始了 PCP 级别的照护，交给训练更少的人就有遗弃的风险。

slides.title: For the BC exam
slides.body:
• Functional enquiry: PCP only, 9 body systems
  • Per system: not asked 5%; missed related info 3%; unrelated 1%
  • Max 15% off; none if no history or the patient is unresponsive
  • Pain history in BC scoring: OPQRRRST or LOTARP
  • Notify the hospital for every exam patient; stroke: en route
  • Book's case gives D50W → BC: D10W only
slides.say: Now the BC exam. In the BC assessment model, the secondary survey includes a functional enquiry, and it's required for PCPs only. It covers nine body systems, from general health and the nervous system through to the skin, the endocrine system, and eyes, ears, nose and throat. For each system, you lose five percent if you don't ask, three percent if you miss information related to the chief complaint, and one percent for unrelated information, up to fifteen percent in total, with no deduction if the patient can't give a history. For pain, BC scoring expects OPQRRRST or LOTARP. And notify the hospital for every exam patient, critical or not; for a stroke, do it en route. And IV glucose in BC is D10W only, not the book's D50W.
slides.sayZh: 现在讲 BC 考试。在 BC 评估模型里，二次评估包括系统问诊，这是 PCP 才要求做的。它涵盖九个身体系统，从全身健康状况、神经系统，到皮肤、内分泌系统，以及眼耳鼻喉。每个系统没问扣百分之五，漏掉与主诉相关的信息扣百分之三，漏掉无关信息扣百分之一，整个系统问诊最多扣百分之十五；病人无法提供病史时不扣分。病人有疼痛时，BC 评分要求用 OPQRRRST 或 LOTARP 口诀。另外，考试中每个病人都要通知医院，不管危重与否；卒中要在途中通知。还有，BC 的静脉葡萄糖只有 D10W，不是书里的 D50W。

slides.title: Three things to remember
slides.body:
1. Report in a fixed order; treatment and response come last
  2. Document every IV, drug and reassessment: not written = not done
  3. Refusing one intervention is still a refusal: informed, witnessed, written

Next: Chapter 20, trauma systems and mechanism of injury
slides.say: Let's wrap up. One: report in the same order every time, and as a PCP your treatment and its response, the IV, the fluid and the drugs, come at the end. Echo every order back. Two: document every IV, every drug and every reassessment, with specifics and times. If it isn't written, you can't prove you did it, and the patient may get a second dose. Three: a refusal of one intervention, like an IV, is still a refusal: a capable patient, informed of the risks, a witness, and a complete record. Next, we start the trauma section with Chapter twenty, trauma systems and mechanism of injury. If anything was unclear, tap Ask. See you next class.
slides.sayZh: 收尾。一，每次都按同样的顺序报告；作为 PCP，你的处置和反应，包括静脉通路、补液和药物，放在最后。每条医嘱都要复述。二，每一次静脉通路、每一种药、每一次复评都要具体记录并写明时间。没写下来就无法证明你做过，病人还可能被重复给药。三，拒绝其中一项处置，比如静脉通路，也是拒绝治疗：病人有行为能力、被告知风险、有见证人、记录完整。下一章开始创伤部分，第二十章：创伤体系与受伤机制。有不懂的点「Ask」。下节课见。
